headline: Cheap AI-made fake images and video are changing how political attack ads are made in the United States.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear trend with counts from two trackers, though the FT article itself was not readable.
importance_line: Voters may see attack ads showing things that did not happen, as in a Republican congressman's ad that appeared to use an AI-altered photo, per HuffPost, but tracker counts differ and use of AI in an ad is not proof of deception.
summary: The Financial Times reports that cheap AI "deepfakes" are giving US political attack ads a new twist, and Fox News Digital reports that the ad-tracking firm AdImpact had counted 29 federal and governor race ads that disclosed AI content by about 21 September, while the Wesleyan Media Project counted at least 164 AI-influenced ads this election cycle, including ads that did not disclose it. Consultants quoted by Fox say AI lets campaigns make in hours what once took days and teams, but it is not yet clear whether it wins elections.
notes: Desk-built entry: FT page is paywalled (HTTP 403), so only its headline is known and it is credited as such. Facts read at Fox News Digital (5 Oct 2026) and HuffPost via AOL (Finstad ad; HuffPost says the image 'appeared to be AI-generated'). Neither is a copy of the FT. Not an exact match for the FT's specific examples.
